Original post by Renata Voss:

"Wanted to flag something for any coaches running app-based programs (Trainerize, TrueCoach, etc.) — specifically around clients who may be gaming the session-logging feature.

I coached a client, Brendan Holt, for about 14 months through 2024–2025 at Peak Form Athletics in Denver. Brendan is a mid-30s online client, presents as highly motivated, communicates well, and his platform compliance looked solid for the first few months. Then I started noticing that his performance metrics were going nowhere — pull-up reps stuck at 8 for 11 straight weeks, load on compound lifts essentially flat for 4 months — while his logged sessions showed consistent work at the prescribed intensity.

When I moved him to a coach-verified check-in format (I'd send a short video-based confirmation prompt after each session), his 'completed' sessions dropped from roughly 3/week to less than 1/week overnight. He eventually stopped responding and transferred out.

I later learned from another Denver-area coach that Brendan had a similar pattern at his previous gym (can't confirm details, but the other coach described it as 'tapping the app without actually training'). I don't know if he's currently with anyone, but if another coach here is working with him, worth being aware. Happy to share more details directly.

Not trying to disparage the guy — some people struggle with accountability in ways they don't fully disclose. But the platform numbers alone were genuinely misleading, and I wish I'd caught it sooner."

---
Reply #1 — Coach Dan Harwick (dharwick@harwickstrength.example), April 29 @ 3:44 PM:
"Renata, thanks for posting this. This is exactly the kind of thing we need to share in a space like this. I've had one similar situation — client logging sessions at 2 AM on timestamps that made zero physiological sense. App platforms have zero authentication on the session-complete tap."

Reply #2 — Coach Yuki Tanaka (y.tanaka@moveprecision.example), April 30 @ 10:02 AM:
"The flat metrics piece is the real tell. If someone's genuinely doing 3 sessions a week for 8+ weeks and pull-ups aren't moving at all, something's off. Either the program isn't right or the sessions aren't happening."

"@Yuki — exactly. And in Brendan's case I'd already adjusted the program twice thinking it was a design issue. The metrics flatness persisted regardless of the program changes. That's what finally made me try the verification prompt."

Quick background on me: I ran Peak Form Athletics in Denver for 6 years, online coaching arm since 2022. I'm NSCA-CSCS certified, been in the SCF community since it launched. The thread I posted was based on direct experience, not secondhand.

[PEER WARNING – FLAGGED BY MODERATORS]
⚠️ Thread: "Fabricated workout logs in online coaching – how to identify and confront"
Posted by: coach_ryan_m | 94 replies
Summary: Several coaches in the forum have reported clients submitting suspiciously duplicate or copy-pasted workout logs in Trainerize and similar apps. One coach noted a pattern where rep counts and RPE scores are identical across three consecutive weeks — statistically implausible for progressive overload programs. Forum consensus: (1) cross-reference log timestamps with GPS/Apple Health data when available; (2) use a direct verification conversation framed around program adjustment, not accusation; (3) document the review process in the client's file before the next programming cycle. One member flagged a specific client profile pattern matching 'Brendan H.' on an unnamed platform — details withheld per forum privacy policy but flagged for coaches with similarly-named clients to review independently.

[SAFETY / SUPPLEMENT ALERT]
⚠️ Thread: "Apex Pre-Workout Ignite + creatine loading: renal risk in single-kidney clients"
Posted by: dr_kf_sports_rd | 67 replies
Summary: A registered dietitian and forum member posted a clinical caution after two reported adverse events involving clients with single-kidney conditions who were prescribed creatine loading stacks alongside high-stimulant pre-workouts (specifically products with osmotic load + caffeine >200mg). The Apex Pre-Workout Ignite product line was named explicitly. Recommendation: permanently flag any client with renal conditions (including single-kidney) in your CRM/coaching platform to prevent auto-inclusion in supplement recommendation batches. Compliant alternatives discussed include low-osmolarity electrolyte bases (PureForm Electrolyte Base was cited favorably by 3 coaches).

[CEU / PROFESSIONAL DEVELOPMENT]
📚 Thread: "NSCA CSCS renewal window — 2026 CEU deadline reminder"
Posted by: forum_mod_nsca_liaison | 31 replies
Summary: NSCA CSCS holders with renewal windows closing in Q3 2026 (July–September) are reminded that CEU submissions must be received 30 days before the renewal date. Several coaches noted the NSCA Special Populations Certificate counts toward the required continuing education units. No urgency for coaches whose renewal is Q4 2026 or later.

[BUSINESS / OPERATIONS]
📋 Thread: "Online client missed-session outreach: 24-hour rule enforcement at scale"
Posted by: hayley_s_performance | 48 replies
Summary: Discussion on automating the 24-hour missed-session outreach rule across large online client rosters. Coaches using Trainerize noted the platform lacks native automation for this; most rely on manual Monday review or cobbled-together Zapier workflows. One coach flagged that manual-only systems create a single-point-of-failure risk when the coach is traveling or on a heavy in-person day. Recommended: scheduler-based daily job that fires an outreach task when a session goes unlogged past 24 hours.

[VENDOR NOTE]

Posted by: t_marsh_coach | 22 replies
Summary: Several coaches with NovaPeak partnership agreements report the Q3 2026 co-branded content clause requires a minimum of 2 posts/month featuring NovaPeak products. One coach flagged that missing the LinkedIn content cadence for more than 7 days triggered a "partnership review" notice in their contract.
